instructions.primary_message: Cut butter into small pieces and set aside to soften.

Line a small rectangular container (we recommend a 6 x 8-inch baking dish, or something similar in dimension) with wax paper, cutting the paper large enough so that it comes up the sides of the container. Set aside.
Pour cream into a small saucepan and bring to a simmer over high heat.
Once the cream has come to a simmer, remove from heat. Add butter, chocolate, and sugar to the hot cream. Using a silicone spatula, gently stir the mixture until chocolate is mostly melted.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ⅓ cups dark chocolate chips
1 tbsp granulated sugar

instructions.primary_message: Add vanilla extract to the pan, then whisk until chocolate is melted and the ganache is smooth and glossy. (Note: If the ganache appears to be "broken" or "separated," continue whisking - it will come back together.)
Pour the ganache into the prepared container and smooth out in an even layer. Press a second piece of wax paper flush against the top surface of the ganache.
Place container in the refrigerator and allow the ganache to set, about 4 hours or up to overnight.
Once the ganache has set, place cocoa powder on a large plate and set aside.

Lift ganache layer out of the container and place on a cutting board. Peel away the top piece of wax paper and discard. Using a sharp knife, cut ganache into 1-inch squares. (If desired, truffles can be shaped into balls by rolling them between your palms.)

Working in batches, transfer squares (or balls) to the plate with the cocoa powder and turn to coat. Dust off excess cocoa powder, then place truffles in mini cupcake liners or arrange on a serving platter (without the liners).
Serve truffles at room temperature. Enjoy!
